next_state_election.name: General and Special Elections
next_state_election.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Virginia's regular voter registration and registration-update deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 23. Eligible voters who miss the deadline may still register and vote in person using a provisional ballot through Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: Early Voting September 18–October 31: Virginia provides no-excuse early in-person voting. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins September 18 and continues through 5:00 p.m. October 31. Local registrar offices and satellite sites provide location-specific schedules.

glance_notes.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any registered Virginia voter may vote absentee by mail without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, a request for a ballot to be mailed must be received by the local registrar by 5:00 p.m. October 23.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Virginia residents may register online through the Virginia Department of Elections Citizen Portal, by mail or in person. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be a resident of Virginia and of the precinct where the person seeks to vote, be at least 18 years old by the next General Election, not currently have been adjudicated mentally incompetent unless competency has been restored, and not have been convicted of a felony unless voting rights have been restored. Virginia also permits eligible voters who miss the regular registration deadline to register and vote provisionally in person through Election Day.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, in person and same-day provisional registration
register.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — How to Register
register.internal_note: Virginia's post-deadline registration procedure is often called same-day registration, but the resulting ballot is provisional and is reviewed before being counted. Virginia felony voting-rights restoration is not automatic under the ordinary voter-registration process; affected applicants must have their civil rights restored before registering.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Virginia's Citizen Portal to check voter registration, update registration information, locate voter-specific election information, apply for an absentee ballot and check absentee-ballot status. Voters should verify their registration and residential address before the election, particularly after moving.
check_registration.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Citizen Portal
check_registration.internal_note: The Virginia Citizen Portal is the state's primary voter-facing system for registration and absentee services.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Virginia's regular deadline to register to vote or update an existing registration is Friday, October 23. Eligible voters who miss that deadline may register in person and cast a provisional ballot after October 23 through Election Day. The provisional ballot is reviewed by local election officials before it is counted.
deadlines.glance_value: October 23; same-day provisional registration available afterward
deadlines.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections
deadlines.internal_note: The Department of Elections expressly lists October 23, 2026 as the General Election registration/update deadline and states that voters may register and vote using a provisional ballot in person after October 23 through Election Day. Do not describe October 23 as an absolute final opportunity to register.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Virginia voters can use the Department of Elections Citizen Portal and polling-place lookup tools to find their assigned Election Day polling place. Early-voting locations are separate and are established by each locality's general registrar, including any authorized satellite locations. Polling locations can change, so voters should confirm their location before voting.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place through Virginia's voter portal
polling_place.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Polling Place Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: Virginia uses assigned precinct polling places on Election Day. Early voting occurs at the general registrar's office and authorized satellite sites rather than the voter's Election Day precinct. Reverify voter-specific locations near November 3.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Virginia's General and Special Elections are Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election Day polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. A qualified voter who is in line at the polling place before 7:00 p.m. is permitted to vote after the closing time if necessary. Voters voting in person are asked to present an acceptable form of identification. A voter without acceptable identification may instead sign an ID Confirmation Statement and vote a regular ballot. A voter who neither presents acceptable identification nor signs the statement must vote a provisional ballot.
election_day.internal_note: Virginia Code § 24.2-603 establishes uniform statewide polling hours of 6:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Voter-ID guidance is important: Virginia does not require a voter who lacks ID to automatically cast a provisional ballot. The voter may sign the ID Confirmation Statement and vote normally.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Virginia polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Election officers identify qualified voters who are in line before the polling place at 7:00 p.m. and permit those voters to vote after 7:00 p.m. if necessary.
polling_hours.internal_note: Current Virginia Code confirms the statewide 6:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. schedule and protects voters already in line before closing.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Any registered Virginia voter may vote early in person without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early in-person voting begins Friday, September 18 and continues through 5:00 p.m. Saturday, October 31. Early voting is available through local general registrar offices and authorized satellite locations. Local schedules vary. For this election, voter registration offices are required to provide early voting on Sunday, October 18; Saturday, October 24; Sunday, October 25; and Saturday, October 31.
early_voting.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections
early_voting.internal_note: Current Department of Elections guidance for the November 3, 2026 General and Special Elections lists early voting from September 18 through 5:00 p.m. October 31 and specifically lists required Sunday voting on October 18 and October 25 plus Saturday voting October 24 and October 31. Exact daily hours and satellite locations remain locality-specific.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Virginia voter may vote absentee by mail without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, a request for a ballot to be mailed must be received by the voter's local registrar by 5:00 p.m. Friday, October 23. A completed absentee ballot returned in person or to an authorized drop-off location must be returned before polls close at 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A ballot returned by mail may be counted if it is postmarked on or before Election Day and received before noon on Friday, November 6. Voters should complete and sign the required voter affirmation on the ballot envelope.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; request by 5:00 p.m. October 23
absentee_mail.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: Virginia Code § 24.2-709 in effect for the November 2026 election provides the late-arriving mailed-ballot rule: postmarked on or before Election Day and received before noon on the third day after the election. November 3, 2026 is Tuesday, making the deadline noon Friday, November 6. In-person and drop-box returns are due by the close of polls. Virginia no longer requires an ordinary absentee voter witness signature under the current voter-affirmation structure; do not copy obsolete witness requirements from older guidance.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Virginia voters casting a ballot in person are asked to show one acceptable form of identification. Accepted forms include a Virginia driver's license or Virginia DMV identification card, U.S. passport, U.S. military ID, qualifying government-issued ID, voter confirmation documents, qualifying student identification, qualifying employee photo identification, certain tribal identification and specified documents showing the voter's name and address. A voter who does not present acceptable identification may sign an ID Confirmation Statement, subject to felony penalties for a false statement, and vote a regular ballot. A voter who neither presents acceptable identification nor signs the statement must vote a provisional ballot.
voter_id.glance_value: Show accepted ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement
voter_id.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — In-Person Voting
voter_id.internal_note: This distinction is critical. Virginia should not be characterized as requiring photo ID. The accepted list includes non-photo documents, and a voter without any acceptable ID can sign the ID Confirmation Statement and vote normally. Virginia DMV driver's licenses and DMV-issued IDs may be current or expired. Most other IDs described as valid generally cannot have expired more than 12 months earlier. Valid student IDs issued by Virginia high schools or higher-education institutions are accepted, as are qualifying photo student IDs from U.S. higher-education institutions.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Virginia provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities. Each polling place and early-voting location must provide accessible voting equipment that allows voters with disabilities to vote privately and independently. Voters may request assistance with voting when eligible and may use curbside voting if they are age 65 or older or have a disability that prevents them from entering the polling place. Virginia also provides accessible absentee-voting options for qualifying voters with print disabilities. Voters needing assistance can contact their local voter registration office or the Virginia Department of Elections.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance, curbside and absentee options
accessible_voting.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Department's current accessibility materials confirm accessible voting equipment, assistance, curbside voting and accessible absentee options. Voters may contact the Department at 800-552-9745 or use Virginia Relay 711. Accessibility-specific email is [adavoter@elections.virginia.gov](mailto:adavoter@elections.virginia.gov).

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Virginia provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible uniformed-service members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may register and submit an absentee-ballot application electronically through Virginia's voter portal when they have the required Virginia DMV identification, or they may use the Federal Post Card Application. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup when applicable. Virginia provides electronic ballot-delivery options for qualifying military and overseas voters. Special deadlines and ballot-return rules apply, so covered voters should follow the Department of Elections' current November 3, 2026 military and overseas instructions.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, FWAB and electronic ballot delivery available
military_overseas.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Military & Overseas
military_overseas.internal_note: The Department has published a specific November 3, 2026 UOCAVA notice. It confirms electronic registration and absentee application through the Virginia portal for voters with qualifying Virginia DMV identification and the FPCA alternative for voters without it. Virginia Code § 24.2-709 provides a separate extended receipt rule for certain covered voters whose ballots were requested on time but were not sent by the statutory ballot-availability deadline. Avoid oversimplifying all UOCAVA ballots to one domestic deadline.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Virginia if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A dormitory or other college address may qualify as the student's voting residence if the student considers it the place where the student resides and intends to remain for an unlimited time. A person may have only one voting residence at a time. Students may vote on Election Day, vote early beginning 45 days before the election or vote absentee by mail. Virginia accepts qualifying student identification for in-person voting, including valid IDs issued by Virginia public or private high schools or institutions of higher education and valid photo student IDs issued by public or private institutions of higher education elsewhere in the United States.
student_voting.glance_value: A qualifying college residence may be used; many student IDs are accepted
student_voting.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — College Student Information
student_voting.internal_note: The Department explicitly states that a dormitory or college address can be an acceptable residential address. Student status alone does not determine residency. Virginia's voter-ID rules are comparatively broad for students: Virginia high-school and higher-education IDs can qualify, and photo IDs from U.S. higher-education institutions can also qualify.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Virginia voters can use the Department of Elections Citizen Portal and official candidate information to determine the contests associated with their registration. Ballots vary by locality and political district. The November 3, 2026 ballot includes federal and local offices, and the Department of Elections currently lists three proposed constitutional amendments for the statewide General Election. Voters should review their voter-specific ballot information close to Election Day because local and special-election contests vary.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check the Citizen Portal and official candidate lists
sample_ballot.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Upcoming Elections
sample_ballot.internal_note: As of August 30, the Department's November 3, 2026 General and Special Elections listing includes U.S. Senate, U.S. House, House of Delegates District 20 Special Election, local general and special elections, and Proposed Constitutional Amendments #1, #2 and #3. Reverify final voter-specific ballot content before publication.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Virginia Department of Elections, Washington Building, First Floor, 1100 Bank Street, Richmond, VA 23219. Toll-free phone: 800-552-9745. Email: info@elections.virginia.gov. Voters with hearing impairments may use Virginia Relay Service at 711. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, early-voting or absentee-ballot questions, contact the appropriate local voter registration office.
contact.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: Current Department materials verify 1100 Bank Street, First Floor, Richmond, VA 23219; 800-552-9745; and [info@elections.virginia.gov](mailto:info@elections.virginia.gov). The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Virginia Department of Elections, Citizen Portal and your local voter registration office for official election information. These resources provide voter registration, registration lookup and updates, polling-place information, early-voting locations, absentee-ballot applications and tracking, voter identification requirements, accessible voting information, military and overseas voting guidance, candidate information and election dates. Virginia's local general registrars administer voter registration, early voting, absentee voting and many local election functions.
official_resources.glance_value: Department of Elections, Citizen Portal & local registrars
